why: Item 1: Check 3 lists every exported function and requires a README heading naming each one (word-boundary regex). A README with padLeft but no slugify section prints "missing: slugify" and fails; the brief also says "slugify had no README section before this change". Item 2: Checks 1–2 only test results that follow from lines 1–2 ("00042", "  ab", "**x", unchanged inputs). Nothing checks the parameter count or that fill is one character; multi-character fill is advisory ("do not fail on it"). Check 3 accepts any heading level, needing only that the heading names the function and has some text under it. That is the plain Markdown idea of a section, not a forced layout. The exact `## name(args)` format appears only in the builder brief. Check 4 only requires npm test to pass. Nothing on the must_not list is present.
